blocks.markdown: A **variable contract** commonly links some policy benefits or values to investment performance. Unlike a traditional policy with only fixed benefits, the value of the investment-linked portion can rise or fall. The Code subjects these products to Insurance Commissioner oversight.

A variable contract's values reflect the investment results of a designated separate account or portfolio. An insurer must first satisfy the Insurance Commissioner about its financial condition and operations. For a foreign insurer, the Code also requires authorization under its home jurisdiction and the stated deposit safeguards.

**Trap.** An insurer cannot present past investment returns as a projection of future performance. Illustrations must follow regulatory rules and must not mislead customers into treating historical returns as guaranteed.

table.caption: Traditional fixed policy vs. variable contract
rows: Policy values/benefits are fixed or determined by the policy’s guaranteed terms, subject to its provisions.
At least part of the policy value/benefit varies with investment results.
Investment performance does not generally directly set the stated benefit.
Investment risk can affect values; review charges, separate account, and product disclosures.
Policy wording and standard Insurance Code rules remain central.
Policy wording plus special Sections 238–246 and Insurance Commission rules matter.
